title: La Porte du Soleil — Storm of Ages
mission: EPIC CINEMATIC EXECUTION MANDATE V1 — unified blueprint over the EXISTING canon (49 scenes / 420 shots / 141 lines). No rewrite, no invented replacement.
canonRelationship: This blueprint ORGANIZES and STAGES the approved F10 story for maximum audience impact. It changes no event, no ending, no dialogue line. Every creative note is tagged SAFE_EDITORIAL or CANON_CHANGING; nothing CANON_CHANGING is applied.
logline: Shipwrecked through a storm into an age of two suns, a young Norse navigator who can read the tides must out-think an Egyptian commander and close a tear between worlds — a door that only a reader can shut, and only from the inside.
chosenDirection: Epic historical action-thriller whose ENGINE is a reader-protagonist: Astrid's power is comprehension, not violence. Action is environmental (the sea/the seam as the weapon) rather than swordplay — this is the film's distinctive, feasible, repeatable signature and its answer to 'action with meaning'. Spectacle serves the mystery (why two suns? who opened the door? what closes it?) and the human cost (who walks in).

actI_SC01_14.arc: Storm → the seam → impossible shore of two suns → captured by Seth-Nakht's guard → the garrison reveals a mystery (Nefer-Ka, the Guardian's wall) and a leash of fear; Olaf is failing.
actI_SC01_14.retentionBeat: By SC14 the audience has the spectacle (storm/seam), the mystery hook (two suns, a debt), the antagonist (Seth-Nakht), and the emotional stake (Olaf's decline, Astrid's self-doubt).

actII_SC15_36.arc: Seth-Nakht's terms → Astrid LEARNS to read (and fails, SC16) → joint evacuations and tides prove her gift publicly → the market tide and his stolen credit → the bleed deepens (two towns, SC25) → canyon echo → third tide → Meryt's confession (the human cause) → the trap clears.
actII_SC15_36.retentionBeat: Rising tide-set-pieces each RAISE the stakes and REVEAL mystery; the midpoint flips Astrid from student to the only one who can read the convergence.

actIII_SC37_49.arc: The suns converge → ASTRID TAKES THE FIELD by calling the tide (SC38, canonical) → Seth-Nakht's authority breaks → the cost (Börk drowns to buy the line, SC40) → two readers, refusals and goodbyes → the close: a reader walks into the seam and shuts it from within, and does not return (SC45/46) → the cairn → an epilogue on a bend in the great river.
actIII_SC37_49.retentionBeat: The climax is a MORAL/INTELLECTUAL victory (she kills his authority, not his men) followed by irreversible loss — excitement resolves into grief and courage.

mysteryLadder.principle: The time-travel rules are revealed progressively through characters, never a title card — keep it comprehensible without over-explaining.

rungs.reveals: SOMETHING tore (the seam) — pure phenomenon, no explanation yet
WHERE/WHEN — an age of two suns; a guarded world with its own order
WHO watches it — Nefer-Ka the reader, the Guardian's wall; a 'leash of fear' Seth-Nakht wields

THE RULES — 'an alignment… the two suns draw close, the wall thins… the debt must be repaid or both ages bleed together… it closes only when someone who can read it walks into it and shuts it from within. It does not return that someone.'
THE CAUSE — Meryt lit the forbidden dawn-rite twice to beg her drowned brother back; 'the suns touched twice; the sky tore wide' — human grief opened the door
THE PRICE PAID — a reader walks in and shuts it; does not return

mysteryLadder.editorialNote: SAFE_EDITORIAL: ensure SH ordering preserves this rung-sequence in the cut; do NOT add a new explanatory line (that would be CANON_CHANGING).

actionDistribution.principle: 17 action-capable scenes (per action-audit-49). The signature is ENVIRONMENTAL action (tide/seam/ground), varied so no two set-pieces repeat. 32 non-action scenes carry character/mystery and are intensified by STAGING ONLY (0 plot change).
actionDistribution.antiRepetitionRule: each tide/seam beat must differ in SCALE, PURPOSE, and Astrid's control-level (learning → proving → commanding → sacrificing). Reuse of identical movement = reject (repetitiveActions guard).
